Alterations (Page 3, clause 0.3) -- Substitute the following for the existing clause: '0.3 The designation of household needles in different sizes adopted in this standard is 15 � 1 system in Catalogue No. 2020. As an alternate, it also incorporates features of system needles classified under 705, 705R and Singer Catalogue Number 2020N needles with rounded sharp point and 2045 with light ball point better suited for sewing synthetics. Comparisons of designation in various systems for household sewing machines needles are given in Appendix A.' (Page 4, clause 5.1 ) -- Substitute the following for the existing clause: '5.1 The dimensions and tolerance for various sizes of needles covered under Catalogue No. 2020 shall be as given in Table 1.' (Page 5, dause 7.2) -- Substitute the following for the existing clause: '7.2 Point -- The point of the needle shall be symmetrical to the centre line of the needle and shall be sharp and well-rounded so that it punches the cloth smoothly without tearing. The shape of the needles shall be as under: a) For 2020 needles -- it shall be sharp set point, Designation: SS; b) For 2020N needles -- it shall be rounded sharp set point, Designation: RS; and c) For 2045 needles -- it shall be light ball point, Designation LB.' (Page 6, clause 8.1, lines 3 and 8) -- Substitute ' Table 3 ' for 'Table 2 ' . (Page 7, Appendix A, value under column 4, against Class 15 � 1 System) -- Substitute ' 16 ' for ' 116'. 1

IS : 2181 - 1973

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR SEWING MACHINE NEEDLES FOR HOUSEHOLD PURPOSES

(First Revision)
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 22 February 1973, after the draft finalized by the Sewing Machines Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on sewing machine and its components prepared at the instance of Development Commissioner for Small Scale Industries, Government of India. This standard was originally issued in 1962. The present revision has been undertaken to take into account one more type of sewing machine needles being manufactured in the country. Accordingly, a unified set of dimensions has been specified. 0.3 The designation for the needle size adopted in this standard is in the Class 15 x 1 System, which is also known as Singer System (Catalogue No. 2020), this system being the most popular system in India. However, for the sake of comparison a chart showing the designation in the Numbering Metric System (International System 705) against that in Glass 15 � 1 System used is shown in Appendix A, for the convenience of users. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observea or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS:2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements of sewing machine needles for household purposes.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised).

3

IS : 2181 - 1973 2. NOMENCLATURE 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the nomenclature of the various parts of the needle shall be as given in Fig. 1.

NOMENCLATURE OF SEWING MACHINE NEEDLE

3. MATERIAL 3.1 The needles shall be manufactured from high carbon needle wire recommended for the needle manufacture. 3.1.1 Typical compositions of two types of steel suitable for needle manufacture are given below: Constituent Percentage Carbon Silicon Manganese Chromium Sulphur Phosphorus 4. HARDNESS 4.1 The hardness of the needle near the steam or centre of flat portion of shank shall be more than 615 HV (see IS: 1501-1968*) or 56 HRC (see IS: 1586-1960). 5. DIMENSIONS 5.1 The dimensions and the tolerances for the various sizes of needles shall be as given in Table 1.
*Methods for Vickers hardners test for steel (first revision). Methods for Rockwell hardness test (B and C scales) for steel (first revision).

6. DESIGNATION 6.1 Needles shall be designated by the appropriate needle site and number of this standard. Example: Needle 14, IS : 2181 7. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 7.1 General -- The needles shall be nickle plated. The surface shall be free from perceptible defects such as sharp edges and burrs specially in the way of the eye. 7.2 Point -- The point of the needle shall be symmetrical to the centre line of the needle and shall be sharp and well-rounded so that it punches the cloth smoothly without tearing.
5

IS 2181 - 1973 8. PERFORMANCE TESTS 8.1 P e r f o r m a n c e -- A needle conforming to this standard when worked with a good quality sewing machine under the sewing conditions as indicated in Table 2 shall meet the following requirements: a) There shall be no breakage of the thread, b) There shall be no skipped stitches, c) Needle shall not get bent, and d) Needle shall not get blunt at the point. Table 2 shows the test conditions for one typical needle size, namely needle No. 14. For different sizes of needles, however, the size and kind of thread, the type of cloth and the number of layers shall be suitably selected.

8.2 Bend Test -- A needle conforming to this standard shall withstand satisfactorily the test given in 8.2.1. 8.2.1 The needle shall be held on its shank in a suitable damp. A gradual load shall be applied at the eye of needle in a direction that the needle bends towards the flat portion of the shank. The application of the load shall be continued till the eye deflects by 4 mm from its original position (see Fig. 2). This position shall be maintained for three seconds after which the load shall be removed. The permanent set, measured at the eye shall not exceed the following limits: Needle size 9 11 14 16 18 19 21 Permanent set, mm 0.08 0.20 0.30 0.35 0.38 0.40 0.40
6

IS : 2181 - 1973

FIG. 2

BEND TEST

9. PRESERVATION AND PACKING 9.1 Needles shall be packed either in oiled paper with a thin foil after being treated with suitable preventive or in vapour phase inhibitor paper (commonly known as VPI paper) or otherwise in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice to prevent exposure to air. 10. MARKING 10.1 Each needle shall be marked with the needle size (as given in Table 1) and the manufacturer's name or trade-mark. The packets shall also be marked similarly. 10.1.1 The needles and/or the packets containing them may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark. 11. SAMPLING 11.1 The sampling plan and criteria for conformity shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.
NOTE -- The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also Continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
